cards.prompt: A clean educational infographic showing a 3-layer neural network with forward propagation (left to right, blue arrows) and backpropagation (right to left, red arrows). Three vertical columns of circles connected by lines: Input layer (4 nodes labeled x) → Hidden layer (6 nodes labeled h) → Output layer (1 node labeled y-hat). Red arrows show error signal delta flowing backward with labels delta3, delta2, delta1. Style: minimal vector illustration on white background, soft blue and red color scheme, no 3D effects, flat design with thin black outlines.

A split comparison infographic: left side shows sigmoid activation function curve (S-shape) with a magnifying glass highlighting the gradient vanishing problem (gradient max 0.25), right side shows ReLU activation function (hockey-stick shape) with a green checkmark highlighting gradient = 1 for positive inputs. Each side has a small tug-of-war metaphor: sigmoid side shows a person with slippery hands (force reduced to 25%), ReLU side shows a person gripping tightly (100% force transmitted). Style: clean vector infographic on white background, warm color palette with soft orange for sigmoid and green for ReLU, flat design, educational diagram style.

An educational bar chart infographic comparing gradient signal transmission ratio across layers. Two groups of bars: blue bars for sigmoid (9%, 10%, 12%, 14%, 16%, 17%) showing severe decay, green bars for ReLU (23%, 29%, 42%, 54%, 61%, 67%) showing much better transmission. A red dashed line at 25% marks the sigmoid theoretical maximum. Bottom caption area shows a simple 2-layer network diagram with arrows showing delta2 to delta1 flow. Style: clean infographic on light cream background, soft pastel colors, minimal flat design, no 3D effects, educational data visualization style.
